rationale: Mercuries Life adopted IFRS 17 from 2026-01-01 and the official 2026Q1 individual financial report retrospectively restated the 2025Q1 comparative period. The original 2025Q1 filing reports basic EPS of positive 0.03, while the 2026Q1 comparative column reports a loss per share of 0.03. The official EPS note reports 5,699,501 thousand comparative weighted-average shares, so the sign change is an accounting-basis restatement and cannot be explained by share-count scaling. Existing 2025Q2, Q3, and annual EPS facts remain from the pre-IFRS-17 reporting basis and cannot be combined with the restated 2025Q1 and 2026Q1 facts to produce a current-comparable TTM EPS or PE.

observations.description: The official auditor emphasis paragraph states that Mercuries Life adopted IFRS 17 from 2026-01-01 and retrospectively restated the 2025Q1 individual financial statements.

The original 2025Q1 filing reports positive basic EPS of 0.03, while the 2026Q1 comparative column reports a loss per share of 0.03. The official comparative weighted-average share count is 5,699,501 thousand, so share scaling cannot explain the sign change.

The official statement of changes in equity and transition note report a 122,647,652 thousand increase in 2025-01-01 equity from retrospective IFRS 17 application, confirming that the accounting-basis change is material rather than a presentation-only relabeling.

The available 2026Q1 filing supplies a restated 2025Q1 comparative, but no same-basis restated 2025Q2 discrete/YTD, Q3 discrete/YTD, or annual EPS facts. Pre-transition 2025 filings therefore remain as-reported evidence only and cannot form a current-comparable TTM series.
